kb.title: Wi-Fi connected but no internet
kb.symptoms: Laptop shows connected to Wi-Fi but websites do not load. Other devices on the same network work.
kb.cause: Stale DHCP lease, bad DNS cache, or a wrong static IP or proxy setting on the laptop.
steps: Turn Wi-Fi off and on, or toggle airplane mode.
Open Command Prompt as admin and run: ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew.
Run: ipconfig /flushdns
Run: netsh winsock reset, then restart the PC.
Settings > Network > Wi-Fi > Hardware properties: make sure IP and DNS are set to Automatic.
Check Settings > Network > Proxy: turn off 'Use a proxy server' unless the company requires it.
If it still fails, test on another SSID or cable to rule out the access point.
kb.prevention: Keep network drivers updated. Do not set static IPs on laptops that move between sites.

kb.title: Outlook stuck on 'Loading profile' or not opening
kb.symptoms: Outlook hangs on the splash screen, shows 'Loading profile', or closes right after opening.
kb.cause: Corrupt profile, damaged add-in, or a large or corrupt OST file.
steps: Start Outlook in safe mode: press Win+R, run outlook.exe /safe. If it opens, an add-in is the cause.
File > Options > Add-ins > Manage COM Add-ins > Go. Untick all, then enable one by one.
Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add a new profile and set it as default.
If the new profile works, remove the old one. The mailbox re-syncs from the server.
As a last step, close Outlook and rename the .ost file in %localappdata%\Microsoft\Outlook so it is rebuilt.
Run the Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant if the problem repeats.
kb.prevention: Keep Office updated and limit add-ins to approved ones.

kb.title: Printer shows offline
kb.symptoms: Printer is on but Windows shows it as Offline, or jobs stay in the queue.
kb.cause: Print spooler stuck, wrong port, or the printer got a new IP address.
steps: Check the printer screen for paper jam, empty tray or error message.
Cancel all queued jobs: Printers & scanners > printer > Open queue > Printer > Cancel all documents.
Run services.msc, restart the Print Spooler service.
Untick 'Use printer offline' in the queue menu if it is ticked.
Print a configuration page on the printer and compare its IP with the port in Printer properties > Ports.
If the IP changed, update the port, or reserve the IP for the printer on the DHCP server.
Remove and re-add the printer as a last step.
kb.prevention: Give network printers a reserved IP address.

kb.title: Computer is very slow
kb.symptoms: Long boot time, applications freeze, fans run loudly.
kb.cause: Low RAM, full or old hard disk, too many startup apps, malware, or pending updates.
steps: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) > Performance. Note which of CPU, Memory, Disk is near 100%.
Memory above 90%: close apps, check the Processes tab, plan a RAM upgrade.
Disk at 100% on an HDD: the fastest fix is replacing it with an SSD.
Startup tab: disable apps you do not need at login.
Free space: clear %temp%, empty the recycle bin, run Disk Cleanup.
Run a full antivirus scan.
Install pending Windows updates and restart. A restart fixes most cases.
kb.prevention: Restart weekly. Use SSDs and at least 8 GB RAM on new devices.

kb.title: Headset or microphone not working
kb.symptoms: No sound in the headset, or the other side on a call cannot hear you.
kb.cause: Muted device, wrong default device, USB port issue, or a driver problem.
steps: Check the mute switch on the headset cable and the volume in Windows.
Right-click the speaker icon > Sound settings and choose the headset as Output and Input.
In the call app (Teams, Zoom) open device settings and select the headset there too.
Try a different USB port and avoid hubs.
Test the headset on another PC or on a phone.
Device Manager: update or roll back the audio driver.
Run the Windows audio troubleshooter (Settings > System > Sound > Troubleshoot).
kb.prevention: Keep one approved headset model to avoid driver differences.

kb.title: Account locked out or forgot password
kb.symptoms: User gets 'Your account has been locked' or the password is not accepted.
kb.cause: Too many wrong attempts, an old saved password on a phone or mapped drive, or an expired password.
steps: Verify the identity of the caller (employee ID and manager name) before anything else.
In Active Directory Users and Computers find the user and open Account. Untick 'Account is locked out' if it is ticked.
If the password expired or was forgotten, reset it and tick 'User must change password at next logon'.
Ask the user to remove the old password from phone mail apps and mapped drives. These re-lock the account.
Log the ticket with the cause and the verification used.
kb.prevention: Remind users to update the password on every device after a change.

kb.title: VPN will not connect
kb.symptoms: VPN client stays on 'Connecting' or shows an authentication or timeout error.
kb.cause: No internet at home, expired password or MFA, blocked ports on the home router, or an outdated VPN client.
steps: Confirm the user has working internet (open any public website).
Ask the user to sign in to the company portal to check the password is still valid.
Check the MFA app time is correct and the code is current.
Restart the VPN client, then reboot the PC.
Try another network such as a phone hotspot. If it works, the home router or ISP blocks VPN traffic.
Reinstall or update the VPN client to the current approved version.
Escalate to the network team with the exact error text and the time it happened.
kb.prevention: Send a password expiry reminder to remote staff.

kb.title: Blue screen (BSOD) after update or at random
kb.symptoms: PC restarts with a blue screen and a stop code such as IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL or PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA.
kb.cause: Faulty driver, bad RAM, failing disk, or a bad Windows update.
steps: Write down the stop code. Do not skip this, it points to the cause.
Boot to Safe Mode (hold Shift while clicking Restart > Troubleshoot > Startup Settings).
If it started after an update: Settings > Windows Update > Update history > Uninstall updates.
If it started after a driver change: Device Manager > roll back the driver.
Run sfc /scannow then DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.
Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched) and check the disk with chkdsk /f.
If it repeats, collect the minidump from C:\Windows\Minidump and escalate or replace the hardware.
kb.prevention: Install drivers from the vendor only and test updates on a pilot group first.

kb.title: Laptop does not charge or turn on
kb.symptoms: No power light, battery stuck at 0%, or 'plugged in, not charging'.
kb.cause: Bad adapter or cable, dead socket, depleted battery, or a stuck power state.
steps: Try another wall socket and check the adapter light.
Swap in a known good adapter of the same wattage.
Unplug everything, remove the battery if removable, hold the power button 30 seconds.
Plug in the adapter only and power on.
Listen for beep codes or watch for blinking LEDs and note the pattern.
Try an external monitor to rule out a dead screen.
If nothing works, open a vendor warranty case with the serial number.
kb.prevention: Do not leave the laptop at 0% for long periods.

kb.title: Windows Update fails or is stuck
kb.symptoms: Update stuck at a percentage, or fails with an error code like 0x80070002.
kb.cause: Corrupt update cache, low disk space, or damaged system files.
steps: Make sure there is at least 20 GB free on C:.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter (Settings > System > Troubleshoot).
Run as admin: net stop wuauserv, net stop bits.
Rename C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution to SoftwareDistribution.old.
Run: net start wuauserv, net start bits, then check for updates again.
Run sfc /scannow and DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth if it still fails.
kb.prevention: Keep free disk space above 15 percent.

kb.title: Mapped network drive missing
kb.symptoms: Shared drive letter is missing or shows a red X in Explorer.
kb.cause: Not on the corporate network or VPN, expired credentials, or group policy not applied.
steps: Confirm the user is on the office network or connected to VPN.
Run gpupdate /force and sign out and in.
Open the share path directly (\\server\share) to test access.
Control Panel > Credential Manager: remove old entries for that server.
Map the drive again and tick 'Connect using different credentials' if needed.
If access is denied, confirm group membership and ask the owner to approve.
kb.prevention: Remind remote users to connect VPN before opening shared files.

kb.title: Monitor shows 'No signal'
kb.symptoms: External monitor is black or shows 'No signal'.
kb.cause: Loose cable, wrong input source, or the PC is not sending a signal.
steps: Check both ends of the cable and power to the monitor.
Press the monitor input button and choose the correct source (HDMI, DP, VGA).
On the PC press Win+P and choose Extend or Duplicate.
Try another cable or port.
Test the monitor with another PC.
Update the graphics driver.
kb.prevention: Label cables and keep spare cables at the desk.

kb.title: Disk full on C: drive
kb.symptoms: Low disk space warning, apps cannot save, updates fail.
kb.cause: Large downloads, temp files, Windows update leftovers, or local copies of mailboxes.
steps: Open Settings > System > Storage to see what takes space.
Run Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files and include Windows Update cleanup.
Clear %temp% and the Downloads folder after asking the user.
Move large personal files to OneDrive or an external drive.
Uninstall unused software.
If the disk is too small for the work, request a larger drive.
kb.prevention: Turn on Storage Sense to clear temp files automatically.

kb.title: Browser shows certificate or 'not secure' warning
kb.symptoms: Chrome or Edge shows 'Your connection is not private' on sites that normally work.
kb.cause: Wrong date and time on the PC, expired site certificate, or a proxy that inspects traffic.
steps: Check the PC date, time and time zone. A wrong clock is the most common cause.
Try the site on another device to see if it is the site itself.
Clear the browser cache and cookies.
Check if the company proxy certificate is installed in the Trusted Root store.
Do not tell users to click 'Proceed anyway' on unknown sites.
Report expired internal certificates to the system owner.
kb.prevention: Keep the PC clock synced with the domain time server.

kb.title: Outlook mailbox full
kb.symptoms: Cannot send or receive email, warning says the mailbox is over quota.
kb.cause: Large attachments and years of mail in the mailbox.
steps: File > Info > Tools > Mailbox Cleanup to see the size per folder.
Empty Deleted Items and Junk Email.
Sort Sent Items by size and remove large attachments.
Use AutoArchive or move old mail to an Online Archive.
If the user needs more space, raise a quota request with manager approval.
kb.prevention: Share large files with links instead of attachments.
